gap: No result ChatGPT got says that these projectors switch to a dimmer Eco mode by themselves when unplugged, or that their quoted battery runtimes are measured in that dim mode. Nebula's own table gives the Mars 3 Air 290 lm in Standard mode but 106 lm in Eco for its 3 hours, and the Mars 3 700 lm in Standard but 300 lm in Eco for its 5 hours. BenQ says the GV50 runs at 70% brightness on battery and is capped at 20% peak brightness on a 45–65 W power bank. XGIMI's MoGo 4 and MoGo 4 Laser take a 65–150 W USB-C PD power bank, but ProjectorCentral reports that the Mars 3 Air uses a proprietary power port.
standout_why: Dupple (2026-11-04) is the only rival whose text I could read. It labels each runtime '(Eco mode)' but gives no battery-mode lumens and no USB-C or power-bank wattage, and its only related line is 'expect less at full brightness' for the JMGO PicoFlix. The two RTINGS pages ChatGPT cited (best/portable and best/under-1000) came back as navigation only, because the article body didn't render, so I couldn't check them. The What Hi-Fi best-portable page also came back truncated. ChatGPT's own answer pairs a plugged-in rating with an Eco-mode runtime, such as 'Mars 3: 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to 5-hour battery in Eco mode', when Nebula's own figure at 5 hours is 300 lm.
decides: If the shopper means running on battery (backyard, camping, travel), the lumen ratings ChatGPT ranked by don't hold. The Mars 3 Air drops to 106 lm (Nebula) or 145 ANSI lm (ProjectorCentral) once unplugged, so it is a poor battery pick even though ChatGPT called it great for backyard movie nights. Unplugged, the Mars 3 still gives 300 lm for 5 hours, so it stays the outdoor pick. For the MoGo 4 / 4 Laser and GV50, the choice depends on extra power: they can run from a USB-C PD power bank (65 W or more for the MoGo; over 65 W for the GV50 to reach full peak brightness and charge while playing). That points to power banks Dealectric already lists, such as the UGREEN 145 W, the AOHi 140 W and the Baseus 100 W.
